head: 4b382e5388e652308d2beca448666630ba6c332d
summary: The change replaces misleading JSON failures with command failures and preserves HTTP status internally at low maintenance cost. Existing output paths still hide that status; live rate-limit benefit and incident frequency remain unknown.
reasons: The focused change replaces misleading JSON errors for empty failed lookups and preserves HTTP status on the internal error. It adds no dependencies, settings, or instructions.
The intended user outcome remains incomplete: Status#required_checks exposes only e.message, and the command boundary prints only e.message. Neither exposes the preserved HTTP status.
The packet reports passing reproduction and full validation, with one review round. Live rate-limit behavior, incident frequency, and observed user benefit remain unknown.
concerns: skills/shaka/lib/shaka/status.rb: Status#required_checks discards http_status and retains the generic required-check message. Maintainers reading status evidence still cannot distinguish rate limiting from other unavailable evidence.

skills/shaka/scripts/shaka.rb: the command error handler prints only e.message. The changed check failure message contains the exit code but no HTTP status or rate-limit cause, so command users do not receive the promised diagnostic.
alternative: Keep the narrow lookup fix and expose a sanitized HTTP status through existing status evidence and command errors. Preserve stderr privacy and existing failure safeguards. The earlier exit-8 coverage finding is a test nit, not a substantive product concern.
next_action: Revise this PR to expose the preserved HTTP status in user-visible check evidence and command errors, with focused boundary tests.
